title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (May 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-05-25 is the last Tuesday of May 2027. The rule is corroborated for MAY specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each read off an April edition fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and verified against its own "Source: April <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and "Updated:" date: CCI-Apr-2023 "The next release is Tuesday, May 30 at 10 AM ET", CCI-Apr-2024 "Tuesday, May 28th", CCI-Apr-2025 "Tuesday, May 27th" -- each of which is the last Tuesday of its May. No May-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified May record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-04-27 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain by which 03-30 proposed 04-27. Proposed for two measured reasons, not bookkeeping. FIRST, it is the CLEAN counterpart that immediately follows this proposer's collision print, and the pair is unusually tight: 2027-04-27 is FOMC day one of the April 27-28 meeting while 2027-05-25 has no Fed meeting anywhere near it (the Fed's posted 2027 calendar runs April 27-28 then June 8-9, so May 2027 is FOMC-free by the same arithmetic the February siblings documented). Two consecutive editions, one colliding and one clean, four weeks apart in one regime is the cleanest within-year collision control this chain has had -- every earlier clean-vs-collision comparison drew its two sets from different quarters. SECOND, and specific to this proposer, MAY is the strongest remaining test of the position-in-month control rule (FT-consumer-confidence-2027-03-30-2/-3). March's width is front-loaded so the month-level control failed there; April's is flat so both controls agreed here; May is the flattest month in the whole sample -- 0 of 9 against the rest of the year, SPY 0.984/0.969, p=0.9446 -- so a month with NO width signature at all is where the two controls should be indistinguishable if the rule is right, and where a divergence would be the rule's clearest falsifier. Note for whichever lane takes it: sourced April cut-off lags run 6/6/8 days, which would put a May-2027 panel at roughly 05-03 -> 05-17, entirely inside the long April-to-June intermeeting window and closing before fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29 begins -- so unlike this proposer, that edition prints in a fully open Fed communication window with no decision in the corridor. Also note memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31 and sifma-bond-early-close-2027-05-28 sit in the week after it. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
